title: Plymouth Road Runner Engines (1968–1980)
description: Every factory engine in the Plymouth Road Runner by year, 1968–1980: the 383, the 440 Six Barrel and 426 Hemi, then the 340, 400 and Volaré-era 318 and 360.
intro: The Road Runner began in 1968 as a low-priced B-body muscle car and ended in 1980 as an appearance and performance package on the compact Volaré.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs, and each row lists the sources that confirm it.

The first Road Runner was built to a price, so its engine list was short: a 383 rated at 335 hp as standard and the 426 Hemi as the option. The 440 with three two-barrels (the A12 package) arrived partway through 1969, and the 1970 Superbird was the only Road Runner offered with the four-barrel 440.

The 1971 redesign kept the Hemi and the 440 Six Barrel for one year. The standard engine was a 400 in 1972 and a 318 in 1973 and 1974, with 340, 360, 400 and 440 options. Ratings are SAE net from 1972.
For 1975 the Road Runner moved to the larger Fury body.
From 1976 the Road Runner was a package on the Volaré coupe with the 318 and 360. The 225 slant six joined in 1979, and the 360 was gone for 1980.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
